Description: Riverside mosque in Daryaganj built on high plinth with black-white striped domes. Citations: Stephen Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'; Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'.
Ornate red sandstone and marble mosque in Kashmiri Gate built in 1728. Citations: Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1847), 'Asar-us-Sanadid'; Swapna Liddle (2011), 'Chandni Chowk: The Shopkeeper's Delight'.

Two triple-arched brick and stone gateways standing on GT Road in Rana Pratap Bagh. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.

Gilded three-domed mosque where Nadir Shah directed the 1739 massacre. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Stephen Blake (1991), 'Shahjahanabad: The Sovereign City in Mughal India'.
Former royal pleasure garden and palace complex north of the old city wall. Citations: Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.
Located near Delhi Gate of Red Fort with gilded copper domes. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'.

Last garden-tomb of Mughal style built for the Vizier of Emperor Ahmad Shah. Citations: Catherine B. Asher (1992), 'Architecture of Mughal India'; Percy Brown (1942), 'Indian Architecture: Islamic Period'.
Gilded-dome neighborhood mosque near modern Central Vista. Citations: Y.D. Sharma (1974), 'Delhi and its Neighbourhood (ASI)'; Lucy Peck (2005), 'Delhi: A Thousand Years of Building'.
Final summer palace built by the last Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar in Mehrauli. Citations: William Dalrymple (2006), 'The Last Mughal'; Swapna Liddle (2018), 'Delhi: 14 Historic Walks'.
